sections.markdown:
## C2 — KG hints for Sharing the Road with Trucks, Trailers, Buses and Motorcycles

FACT_ID: sec16-R01 | anchor: A01
A large vehicle's driver sees farther ahead than a car driver, while the sides, the rear and especially the area immediately behind are blind except through mirrors [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint large-vehicle-limits; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec16-F04 and sec16-F06.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-R02 | anchor: A03
A trailer needs its own brakes when it exceeds half the tow vehicle's weight or three thousand pounds, while every trailer regardless of weight needs safety chains fixed to the frames [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint towing; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec16-F15 and sec16-F17.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-R03 | anchor: A04
Too much weight on the hitch makes the tow vehicle hard to steer, while too little makes the trailer fishtail, so ten to fifteen percent of the trailer weight is the target [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint towing; prereq_hint sec16-R02; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec16-F19 and sec16-F18.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-R04 | anchor: A06
A motorcycle's small size makes it look farther away and slower than it is, while its maneuverability lets it appear suddenly in places a driver cannot see [A06].
Why it matters: group_hint motorcycle-perception; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec16-F22 and sec16-F25.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec16-R05 | anchor: A07
A rider moving to one side of the lane may be preparing a turn or dodging a hazard, while a blinking motorcycle signal may be a forgotten one, so only an unmistakably started maneuver reveals intent [A07].
Why it matters: group_hint motorcycle-intent; prereq_hint sec16-R04; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec16-F28 and sec16-F24.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec16-R06 | anchor: A09
When a motorcycle passes you, you hold your lane and speed, while when you pass a motorcycle you give it a full lane and do not return early [A09].
Why it matters: group_hint motorcycle-passing; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec16-F31 and sec16-F32.
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec16-R07 | anchor: A02
Large vehicles need more distance to stop and more room to turn, while they also accelerate slowly and may travel below the limit, so both following and passing need extra margin [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint large-vehicle-limits; prereq_hint sec16-R01; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec16-F07 and sec16-F08.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-R08 | anchor: A02
A large vehicle's downgrade danger is brake fade, answered by a lower gear, while its slipstream danger is a wind gust that pushes smaller vehicles sideways [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint large-vehicle-limits; prereq_hint sec16-R07; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec16-F09 and sec16-F10.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-R09 | anchor: A08
Two seconds is the minimum gap behind a motorcycle, while an even larger gap is advised because the rider's speed and distance are hard to judge [A08].
Why it matters: group_hint motorcycle-following; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec16-F29 and sec16-F30.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec16-R10 | anchor: A05
Motorcyclists are more vulnerable to injury than car drivers in a crash, while over two thirds of crashes between cars and motorcycles happen when a car driver turns in front of the motorcyclist [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint motorcycle-intersections; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec16-F21 and sec16-F27.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec16-R11 | anchor: A03
A large trailer that blocks the inside mirror requires outside mirrors on both sides, while a house trailer may never carry passengers [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint towing; prereq_hint sec16-R02; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec16-F14 and sec16-F16.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-R12 | anchor: A02
Hazardous-material trucks must be marked so responders know the cargo, while emergency equipment such as extinguishers and flares is carried on most large vehicles whatever the cargo [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint large-vehicle-duties; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec16-F11 and sec16-F12.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0086]
